title: Dual-view Molecular Pre-training

problem.claim: Molecular pre-training seeks effective molecular representations from large amounts of data.

contributions.claim: The work proposes dual-view molecule pre-training (DVMP), combining molecular graph and SMILES-sequence representations.
DVMP uses Transformer and GNN branches that are pre-trained to maintain molecular semantic consistency.
After pre-training, DVMP supports using the Transformer branch, the GNN branch, or both for downstream tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: DVMP outperforms strong baselines on 11 molecular property prediction tasks.
DVMP achieves state-of-the-art results on three retrosynthesis tasks.
The authors report releasing the code publicly.

narrative_sequence.summary: Molecular pre-training is presented as an active approach for learning molecular representations from large datasets.
Molecules can be represented as graphs or SMILES sequences, with GNNs and Transformers modeling these views in complementary ways.
DVMP combines the two views through Transformer and GNN branches trained for semantic consistency.
The method is evaluated on molecular property prediction and retrosynthesis tasks, with reported gains over baselines and state-of-the-art results.

source_observation.claim: The method combines graph and sequence representations through separate Transformer and GNN branches.

interpretation.claim: Maintaining consistency across complementary representations may support a more flexible molecular pre-training framework.

application.claim: For domains with multiple complementary data representations, consider jointly pre-training specialized branches with a consistency objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers to domains or tasks beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the pre-training dataset, task datasets, evaluation metrics, or baseline identities.
The abstract does not quantify the reported improvements or describe ablations.
The abstract does not provide implementation, training, or reproducibility details beyond a code-release statement.
